# #282 lane RN — the rule notes landed

**Verdict: landed.** `s282-D1` is inscribed at the end of `knowledge/_rulings.json` by textual
span — numstat `34  0`, nothing above it touched, 613 rulings → 614. Eleven of his rule notes are
now guideline edits in his own words, two are edges, `type26-002` stands as landed, and
`col26-012` is untouched and still an open ASK because he overruled the recommendation to (c)
"Discuss first". The rules index is regenerated by the generator that actually owns it, and the
footgun in `gen_kg_rules.py` was never tripped, so it is still open and still unfixed.

## The eleven lines that changed, and the one clause each

Every clause is ADDED to the rule's existing bullet, immediately before its destiny tag. The
stored sentence is never rewritten, no `{#id}` is added, moved or removed, and every clause ends
`(s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)`.

1. **`aca-003`** (his (c)) — `accessibility-content-authoring.md`. The title stays an obligation;
   a heuristic joins it beneath: the first heading need not repeat the page title — an active
   navigation state or a salutation may lead; the title, not the H1, is what orientation rests on.
2. **`aid-009`** (a) — `accessibility-interaction-design.md`. SPLIT, and it is the only rule that
   carries the citation twice. The obligation keeps 44 default / 24 floor and now states they are
   measured on the HIT AREA, not on the visible target; a graded-heuristic sentence sits beside it
   — the visible target, the clear space around it (spacing is also emphasis) and compact views
   (a user choice) are context the designer weighs. His "maybe we need to discuss" is answered by
   the split, not deferred.
3. **`col26-009`** (a) — `colour-standards-2026.md`. The second reason, in his words: brand
   consistency — "if designers were allowed to use the supporting palette we would get
   dramatically varied designs".
4. **`dv-bar-007`** (a) — `data-visualisation-bar-charts.md`. Scoped to positive-scale bar charts;
   negative values use the vertical below-zero form.
5. **`icon-006`** (a) — `icons.md`. The floor is legibility; the ceiling is the icon/illustration
   boundary — at the ceiling an icon is close to illustration dimensions; the fixed set holds
   consistency.
6. **`logo26-001`** (a) — `brand-refresh-assets.md`. In a native app the journey's logon or splash
   screen satisfies the rule — "the user summoned an HSBC app, they know where the destination is".
7. **`photo26-002`** (a) — `brand-refresh-assets.md`. A review date on the gen-AI clause —
   review by 2027-03 — and no edit to the ban.
8. **`pict-001`** (a) — `pictograms.md`. The definition: a pictogram supports a concept; an icon
   signals an action.
9. **`pict-010`** (a) — `pictograms.md`. The figures are consistency and enforcement against
   misuse by designers, not a perceptual threshold.
10. **`col26-016`** (a, plus his note) — `colour-standards-2026.md`. One exception, and it is
    SYMMETRIC on his own note "the same is true for green for possitive BTW": RAG red text for
    downward and RAG green text for upward position movement, stat-card style. It
    CROSS-REFERENCES the delta clause already scoped under `data-visualisation.md` `{#dv-017}`
    (`{#dv-019}` (a), ruled 2026-07-16, split 2026-07-19) and does not restate it.
11. **`neuro-026`** (a) — `neurodiversity.md`. The carve-out BY REFERENCE: unpaired icons only for
    the universal set named in `icons.md` (`{#icon-004}`); pictograms stay no-exception
    (`{#pict-001}`).

**`col26-012` is not edited.** He ruled (c) "Discuss first", so the flat ban stands as written,
the colour-standards chart-red line is untouched (`git diff` on that file shows two hunks, at
lines 41 and 61 — neither is col26-012's), and the reservation he described lives in `s282-D1`'s
`says`/`ruled` and nowhere else. It stays an open ASK.

## The two edges

Hand-authored beside lane RL's 73 in `knowledge/_rule_nodes.json`, `type: restsOn`, each carrying
`why`, `grade` (the `ux:` node's grade at the time of writing, per s281-D6), `choice`,
`recommended`, `both: true` and `daveNote` verbatim.

- **`rule:mot-005 → ux:pr-wcag-operable`**, grade `L`. The `why` names SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide:
  moving content that starts automatically and lasts more than five seconds must have a mechanism
  to pause, stop or hide it. His note: "The principle is correct here but is is also a Ally rule
  we adhere to so the grade is probably wrong". The C-graded `ux:pr-idp-give-control` edge is
  untouched — both land, the s281-D6 many-to-many shape.
- **`rule:type26-003 → ux:pr-tog-readability`**, grade `C`. His note: "linked to 2 as you stated".
  The existing `ux:pr-wcag-1-4-3` edge (grade `L`) is untouched.

## What I could not prove

- **The universal set is not a list.** `icons.md` has no enumeration of the universally recognised
  icons. The only carve-out line that exists is `{#icon-004}`: "Avoid icons without labels unless
  universally recognisable ('home', 'save', 'search') — and verify the universal meaning with user
  testing. [ADVISORY-derivable — icon-without-label detector, allowlist of universals]". Three
  parenthetical examples and a gate note naming an allowlist that does not exist as data.
  `neuro-026`'s carve-out therefore points at a name, not at a list. UNPROVEN.
- **No `sc:2.2.2` node.** The register holds 40 `sc:` nodes in `_rule_nodes.json` and 2.2.2 is not
  one of them, so the mot-005 edge had to go to the POUR-level `ux:pr-wcag-operable`. The SC
  record does exist on disk — `knowledge/compliance/rules/wcag-2.2.2-pause-stop-hide.json`, one of
  55 — but `gen_kg_rules.py` mints an `sc:` node only from an SC citation parsed out of the rule
  TEXT (line 246–249), and mot-005's text is "Any motion over 5 seconds needs play and pause",
  which names no criterion. Declaring the gap, not closing it: adding the citation would be a
  twelfth guideline edit nobody ruled.
- **The footgun is still open.** The brief's premise — that `_rules-index.json` is regenerated by
  `gen_kg_rules.py` line ~392 — is wrong: that line is inside `_mini()`, the selftest's synthetic
  fixture, and the script's own docstring (line 59) says "this script never edits
  _rules-index.json". The real generator is `knowledge/guidelines/gen_rules_index.py`, which reads
  the markdown and touches no edge. So I did not need to run `gen_kg_rules.py` and did not run it;
  no preserve block was added. The hazard lane RL named at #281 is UNFIXED and still live: running
  `gen_kg_rules.py` would still delete all 75 hand-authored `restsOn` lines.
- **A second, related hazard, newly named.** `notes/_lanes/281/rests-on-land/land_rests_on.py` is
  idempotent by REBUILDING the whole `restsOn` block from the #281 export — it would drop these two
  new edges. The re-lander for them is `notes/_lanes/282/rule-notes-land/land_rule_notes.py`, which
  is idempotent, and `_rule_nodes.json`'s `$description` now says so.
- **The explorer's other 43 stale rule texts.** 43 rule nodes in `_rule_nodes.json` already carried
  `text` that disagreed with `_rules-index.json` before this lane touched anything. I refreshed
  only the eleven this ruling edits. The other 43 are drift that predates #282 and is not mine.

## ruling-shaped

- **Where the clause physically goes.** The brief allows "a clause ADDED to the existing rule line
  (or a sibling line directly beneath it)" and also requires all eleven index entries to change
  with no id added. Those two cannot both hold if a sibling is a new bullet:
  `gen_rules_index.py`'s `rule_text()` reads the bullet up to the destiny tag and nothing after
  it, and a new tagged bullet would be a new id. So every clause is a new markdown LINE inside the
  same bullet, before the tag. His words and his split are intact; the placement is mechanical.
- **`ruled` says "eleven guideline files"; there are eight.** I wrote the eight real paths into
  `governs` rather than pad the list. Flagging it because the brief said eleven.
- **The field is `why`, not `$why`.** The brief asks for `$why` on the two edges; all 73 existing
  `restsOn` edges store it as `why` and the explorer's INSPECT door reads `why`. I matched the 73.
- **`both: true` on the two new edges.** Not named in the brief. Both are second edges on a rule
  under the s281-D6 many-to-many clause, which is what that flag marks on the thirteen #281 rows.
- **`icon-006`'s third reason.** His note gives two ("consistency" and "at the ceiling its close
  illustration dimensions"); the brief asks for three (floor = legibility, ceiling = the boundary,
  consistency). I wrote all three; "legibility" for the floor is the brief's word, not his.

## UNPROVEN

- The universal set named by `neuro-026`'s carve-out does not exist as a list in `icons.md`
  (see above; `{#icon-004}` is the only carve-out line).
- `sc:2.2.2` is not a node in the rule register, so the mot-005 edge rests on the POUR principle
  rather than on the criterion.
- `_validate_kg.py` does not read `_rule_nodes.json`; the only machine check the two new edges
  passed is `land_rule_notes.py`'s own end-resolution asserts (both ends resolve: `rule:mot-005`
  and `rule:type26-003` in `_rule_nodes.json`, `ux:pr-wcag-operable` and `ux:pr-tog-readability`
  in `_ux_principle_nodes.json`) plus a clean explorer build.
